desc:
Find the shortest contiguous subarray of nums such that sorting just that subarray in non-decreasing order makes the whole array sorted in non-decreasing order. Return its length, or 0 if the array is already sorted.

Examples: [2, 6, 4, 8, 10, 9, 15] gives 5 (sort [6, 4, 8, 10, 9]); [1, 3, 2, 2, 2] gives 4; [1, 2, 3, 4] gives 0.
hints: Sorting a copy and comparing it with the original shows the first and last mismatch, which gives an O(n log n) answer. Can you find these two positions in O(n)?

The right end of the window is the last index whose value is smaller than the maximum of everything before it. The left end is the first index whose value is larger than the minimum of everything after it.
Scan left to right keeping the running maximum and mark end = i whenever nums[i] is below it. Scan right to left keeping the running minimum and mark start = i whenever nums[i] is above it.
editorial: An element is out of place on the right side if something larger precedes it, so the rightmost such element marks where the window must end: scanning left to right with the running maximum, the last index with nums[i] < max is the end. Symmetrically, an element is out of place on the left side if something smaller follows it, and the leftmost such index (found by scanning right to left with the running minimum) is the start.

If no index is ever below the running maximum the array is sorted and the answer is 0. Otherwise the answer is end - start + 1. Equal values are never counted as out of order because the comparisons are strict, which is why [1, 3, 2, 2, 2] needs the window [3, 2, 2, 2] but [1, 2, 2, 3] needs nothing.
